thread:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired for service=redwood-api-prod (high error rate, tls failures)

pagerduty-bot: INCIDENT TRIGGERED: PD-4521 · redwood-api-prod · P1 · triggered by Alarm: ALB-TargetHealth-FailedThreshold
pagerduty-bot: link: https://pagerduty.example/PD-4521

raj: oncall here, ACKing the page. jumping in.
ashley: acked — looking at ALB metrics now. seeing spike in 5xx and TLS handshake errors from eu-west-1 targets.
maria: I'm pulling target group health checks. one target in eu-west-1 marked Unhealthy, failing TLS handshake.

kevin: support reports customers in EU are seeing connection resets & "ERR_SSL_PROTOCOL_ERROR" in browser.
raj: timeline: started ~2026-03-14T03:12Z per alert. rolling error rate up to ~18% for /v1/generate calls.

ashley: quick checks: `aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:aws:...:tg/eu-west-1/abc123`
```
ashley: TARGET HealthDescriptions:
  - ip: 10.0.4.12 state: unhealthy reason: TLS handshake failure
  - ip: 10.0.5.33 state: healthy
```

maria: tls logs from the backend show SNI mismatch for connections from ALB -> backend. certificate served by backend process is for `internal-service.local`, not `api.redwood.cloud`.
raj: that's odd. we rotated certs last week but only for edge. maybe a deploy picked up a wrong config. any recent deploys to eu cluster?
kevin: deploy bot shows a canary rollback 02:58Z in eu-west-1 for `runtime-service` with a config patch.

ashley: I'm looking at the runtime-service pod env: `TLS_CERT_PATH=/etc/tls/internal.pem` — that looks wrong. should be `/etc/tls/api-prod.pem`.
maria: if backend serves wrong cert, ALB will see handshake fail -> 502/526 from clients. we need to route traffic away from affected target(s) while we fix cert.

raj: mitigation plan: 1) mark unhealthy targets OutOfService in TG to stop ALB sending them traffic 2) update deployment to point to correct cert 3) test and bring back 4) if DNS/edge TTLs cause client cache issues, announce temporary mitigation.

ashley: executing step 1: `aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn ... --targets Id=10.0.4.12`
incident-bot: Executed deregister-targets (simulated). target 10.0.4.12 now draining.

maria: telemetry shows error rate dropping to ~6% after draining that target. good signal.

raj: creating an incident record: https://incidents.redwood/INC-2026-103 · severity=P1 · impacted=production eu region.

kevin: posting customer-facing note to status page draft: "We are investigating an issue affecting some EU customers with TLS handshakes resulting in failed requests. Working on mitigation and will update shortly."
ashley: step 2: patching runtime-service deployment to load correct TLS path and rolling restart in eu namespace. applying manifest now.
```
ashley: kubectl -n eu apply -f runtime-service-fixed-cert.yaml
```

maria: verifying pod cert after restart: `openssl s_client -connect 10.0.5.33:8443 -servername api.redwood.cloud` -> certificate CN=api.redwood.cloud ✓

raj: observing latency and error dashboards. error rate down to baseline ~0.8% and TLS handshake errors almost zero.

kevin: support update: "We've seen a drop in reports after 03:40Z — telling customers to retry, clearing browser caches if needed."

ashley: step 3: re-register drained target after successful healthcheck: `aws elbv2 register-targets ... Id=10.0.4.12`
incident-bot: register-targets executed; target health is now healthy.

raj: root cause draft: misconfigured cert path during a canary rollback caused backend to serve internal cert in eu cluster, causing ALB->backend TLS failures.

maria: immediate follow-ups: 1) add a preflight check in deploy pipeline that verifies server certificate CN matches expected SNI 2) add ALB->backend TLS alert for SNI mismatch 3) run cross-region cert consistency check weekly.
kevin: ops follow-up tasks created in TODO board: TODO-5412, TODO-5413, TODO-5414.

ashley: resolving incident now in PagerDuty (PD-4521) and posting final incident note.
pagerduty-bot: PD-4521 status: resolved by raj at 03:55Z (ack->resolve).

raj: handing off to morning SRE oncall @ashley for follow-ups. I'll add ops notes and close my active pager.
ashley: got it — will own postmortem and follow-ups.

kevin: support note posted to customers at 04:05Z.

maria: monitoring for 1h after resolution. will escalate if regressions.

raj: thanks everyone. postmortem owner=ashley. severity=P1; customer-impact=partial (eu region, some customers saw failed requests and TLS errors).

ashley: filing postmortem draft: https://docs.redwood/postmortems/INC-2026-103-draft

incident-bot: Thread archived after resolution. :white_check_mark:"
